summary: POC scoping call to decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer goal: embed LLM capabilities into internal tooling with strict PII controls, sub-200ms p95 latency for chat, and predictable monthly costs. Agreed pilot: 2-week hosted benchmark followed by decision to move to Dedicated or Private if needed for latency/residency. Action items: share dataset, schedule benchmark run, deliver pricing and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick intros, I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. Lena with me is our SE.
[00:00:12] Aisha: Hi, I'm Aisha, head of ML at Pioneer Labs, Tom is on platform and Marta is security. Thanks for doing this.
[00:00:20] Lena: Great, thanks. High level for today we want to scope the POC — success criteria, workloads, benchmarks, and then talk deployment modes: hosted, dedicated, private and what would push you one way or another.
[00:00:35] Tom: Yep that sounds good. Our main constraints are data residency for some datasets, and p95 latency needs to be under ~200 ms for our internal chat assist, otherwise it's too slow for users.
[00:00:48] Aisha: Also cost — we need predictable monthly spend; startup budgets are tight so per-token surprises are tough.
[00:00:55] Samir: Understood. Quick question on workload sizing — can you give ballpark qps and average token sizes?
[00:01:05] Aisha: For phase one it's pretty small: about 1,000 queries/day for the chat pilot, average prompt length 120 tokens, responses average 80 tokens. We also plan embeddings for search — roughly 10k docs, embedding batch jobs nightly, embedding vector dim 1536.
[00:01:23] Tom: Peak concurrency we'll see maybe 15 concurrent users, so 15 qps burst, sustained probably 0.2 qps.
[00:01:32] Lena: That's helpful — sounds like latency is a primary SLO and cost predictability is a primary business constraint. For that profile you can start with hosted for fast time-to-value and run a benchmark to measure p50/p95 and token cost.
[00:01:44] Marta: What's the difference in data handling between hosted and dedicated/private? We need to know about retention and whether logs or payloads leave our VPC.
[00:01:54] Samir: Good question. Hosted keeps data in our environment but we do process requests on shared infra; we have strict data controls, can enable data retention off for the customer so we don't persist payloads. For dedicated you get reserved capacity and isolated GPU pools — data flows through your tenant but remains under Redwood tenancy; for private you get customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem — that provides the strongest data residency guarantees.
[00:02:18] Marta: And KMS? We want to manage keys for encryption at rest.
[00:02:23] Lena: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports customer-managed keys for some enterprise tiers, but generally private/dedicated are easier for custom KMS policies. I'll follow up with our KMS integration notes.
[00:02:35] Aisha: From success criteria perspective, we'll judge: 1) latency (p95 <200 ms for chat), 2) quality parity with our baseline (we use a small in-house tuned model), 3) cost under a threshold monthly, and 4) security checklist items (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs).
[00:02:53] Samir: Perfect — that's clear. For the pilot we typically run a two-week hosted benchmark where we replay a representative workload and measure throughput, p50/p95, cost per token, and cache hit rates. If hosted meets latency and security requirements we recommend staying hosted. If latency or residency is an issue we discuss Dedicated (predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools) or Private for on-prem/VPC.
[00:03:14] Tom: One of our concerns is network egress latency when users are in EU and model region is US. Does Redwood have multi-region routing?
[00:03:23] Lena: Yes — we have smart routing and region pinning. For hosted we can select EU region endpoints for lower latency; for Dedicated you can provision capacity in a specific region, and Private is entirely under your network so you control locality.
[00:03:34] Aisha: For the embedding batch, is there a recommended quantization or batching approach to save cost?
[00:03:40] Lena: Yes we recommend batching and using optimized quantized variants for embeddings if your quality tolerance allows. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles based on sample inputs. For nightly jobs you can use larger batch sizes and tolerate longer runtimes to minimize cost.
[00:03:52] Marta: On compliance, we need audit logs and RBAC for model access. Can those be exported to our SIEM?
[00:03:58] Samir: Audit logs and tracing hooks are available; we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure connectors for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports webhook and export for enterprise tiers.
[00:04:10] Aisha: Good. Let's talk benchmarks — what's your typical p95 numbers for the models we might use? We're testing a 7B-ish model variant for cost reasons.
[00:04:20] Lena: For a quantized 7B variant on A100-class hardware p50 might be ~30-60 ms per token and p95 depends on sequence length and batching; for chat sequences like yours the end-to-end p95 target of 200 ms is tight but achievable with region-local hosted or dedicated with reserved capacity and smaller sequence lengths. We'll run the benchmark to be precise.
[00:04:39] Tom: If we move to Dedicated, what's the commit structure and how quickly can we spin up capacity?
[00:04:45] Samir: Dedicated is typically a reserved monthly commit; we do short-term eval pockets though — we can provision a small dedicated pool for pilot benchmarking within a week depending on capacity. For Private on-prem it takes longer — 4–8 weeks usually for install and networking.
[00:04:57] Aisha: Timeline-wise we want to decide by end of March. So a two-week hosted benchmark in mid-March fits. If hosted fails latency or residency tests we'll need a path to get Dedicated ready by April.
[00:05:10] Samir: That aligns — propose this timeline: 03/09 start hosted benchmark (two weeks), 03/23 review results; if we need Dedicated, provision in early April, target production pilot in mid-April.
[00:05:21] Marta: What about costs — do you have a model for comparing hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved cost?
[00:05:28] Samir: We'll send a cost model spreadsheet but high-level: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token and is best for small/variable workloads; Dedicated is more cost-effective at scale and provides predictability. For your 1k/day chat and nightly embeddings, Hosted may be cheaper initially; Dedicated becomes attractive if your throughput or latency needs increase.
[00:05:44] Lena: Also consider caching and batching — prefix/KV caching reduces token volumes for repeated prompts which improves hosted economics too.
[00:05:52] Aisha: Good point. For the benchmark data we'll share some typical chat transcripts and the nightly embedding job profile. Anything else you need?
[00:05:58] Samir: Please include error cases and max sequence lengths in the sample set. We'll build a replay harness to simulate bursts and long-tail cases.
[00:06:08] Tom: For the benchmark run, can we measure tail latencies and token cost per request?
[00:06:11] Lena: Yes — our benchmark reports p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost per token, cache hit rates, and KV cache effectiveness. We'll also measure CPU/GPU utilization in Dedicated so you can plan capacity.
[00:06:23] Marta: On security paperwork, we need SOC2, ISO, and penetration test summaries.
[00:06:28] Samir: We'll include SOC2 and our pen test summary; for ISO we can share the certificate or attestations we have. Lena will share the security docs link after the call.
[00:06:38] Aisha: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[00:06:41] Lena: Potential gotchas: 1) Model mismatch — quality differences between tuned in-house and open variants can require additional prompt engineering; 2) warm-up / cold start costs — first few requests may be higher latency until kernels and KV cache warm up; 3) network egress for private datasets — need to validate region and egress policies.
[00:06:58] Tom: For private on-prem physics — do you have an installer or is it a managed appliance?
[00:07:04] Samir: We have a private deployment package and partner-assisted installs; it's not fully appliance-based but can be adapted. Typical timeline as mentioned 4–8 weeks including network and KMS integration.
[00:07:15] Aisha: Let's recap then.
[00:07:18] Samir: Recap: Pioneer will share dataset + workload profile by 03/09. Redwood will provision hosted benchmark starting 03/09 for two weeks. Redwood to send pricing/SOW and security docs by 03/06. Bench results review 03/23. If hosted meets p95 <200 ms and security checks pass, proceed on hosted. If not, evaluate Dedicated with provisioning targeted early April or Private if residency requires.
[00:07:40] Marta: That works. One more small ask — can you include sample RBAC role definitions for model access?
[00:07:46] Lena: Yes I'll include sample RBAC and an example audit log export format.
[00:07:50] Samir: Perfect. Quick note — we'll also attach a link to a short benchmark runbook and a pricing worksheet after the call.
[00:07:58] Aisha: Sounds good, thanks.
[00:08:00] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the benchmark.
[00:08:04] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" split, sample names). Shared artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-runbook, https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf, https://redwood.example.com/pricing/pioneer-worksheet.xlsx
